correctness.rationale: Explicit definitions and finite quantifiers: exactly 16 graph vertices and 24 edges; complex generated by precisely all 33 perfect matchings. The supplied standard-library verifier reconstructs all 6051 nonempty faces and all 27192 Hasse covers, checks a 3019-pair matching and completes an acyclic topological sort. It computes the exact signed integral gradient-path Morse boundary for all eight critical three-cells and obtains the zero 4x8 matrix. With one critical zero-cell, no one-cells, four two-cells and eight three-cells, Hurewicz identifies attaching maps with their degree vectors and gives the claimed wedge equivalence. Independent GF(2) boundary ranks and matching-extension census support input integrity but are not substituted for the integral proof. Actual standalone verifier ended VERIFY_OK.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Bayer and collaborators prove results for finite planar honeycomb patches. Chandrakar–Singh treat polygonal linear tilings. Agarwal–Basak treat opposite-edge Möbius ladders and circular ladders, not the girth-six GP(8,3) graph. The known Heawood perfect-matching homotopy theorem concerns a different graph. The published GP(8,3) ordinary matching homotopy theorem does not classify subcomplex inclusions. None of their hypotheses or conclusions implies the stated four-plus-eight wedge for this object.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches of indexed mathematical findings and primary literature, together with material reading of the exact-graph ordinary matching classification, the exact-graph matching-polynomial paper, and relevant perfect-matching topology papers, did not reveal a homotopy classification of the strict perfect-matching complex of GP(8,3). The closest exact-graph result classifies the ordinary complex with 11067 faces and wedge dimensions four and five; the new strict extendibility complex has 6051 faces and different dimensions. Matching-polynomial coefficients do not encode incidence maps. Planar honeycomb, polygon-line and Möbius-ladder homotopy results are inapplicable on their graph hypotheses. This is a bounded best-knowledge novelty assessment, not an exhaustive uniqueness guarantee.

value.rationale: The Möbius–Kantor graph is canonical among symmetric cubic graphs; perfect matching extendability supplies a natural subcomplex of its already studied ordinary matching complex. The pure seven-dimensional complex has a genuinely mixed wedge of lower-dimensional spheres, with its full integral homotopy—not merely ranks—proved. The known ordinary complex has wedge dimensions 4 and 5 rather than 2 and 3; 112 minimal nonextendible triples and 120 minimal nonextendible quadruples explain a concrete structural change. The older 33-facet count alone cannot determine this invariant. The exact single-graph classification is a meaningful missing entry, without asserting a general downstream theorem.
